column1: # Fray N., Schmitt B. (2009). Sublimation of ices of astrophysical interest: A bibliographic review.
# Planetary and Space Science 57, 2053-2080. DOI 10.1016/j.pss.2009.09.011 (paywalled; not read).
# Reproduced in: Lisse C.M. et al. (2020), "On the Origin & Thermal Stability of Arrokoth's and Pluto's Ices",
# arXiv:2009.02277v1, Supplementary Online Material, Appendix, "Table 2 - Coefficients of the polynomials of
# extrapolations ln(Psat) = A0 + sum Ai/T^i, from Fray & Schmitt 2009", printed page 35 (PDF page 35 of 36).
# Local copy: ../fray-schmitt-2009/arxiv-2009.02277.pdf (sha256 a5d1b01a00c9126ae48fe64f9dbe2b27cc3f9286b8b222c1a2c872091c4641ea).
# Functional form: ln(Psat) = A0 + A1/T + A2/T^2 + A3/T^3 + A4/T^4 + A5/T^5 + A6/T^6, T in K.
# Units of A_i: K^i as printed. The pressure unit is NOT printed in the reproduction. Fray and Schmitt work in bar, and
# CO2-1 gives 1.008 bar at 194.6855 K (the normal sublimation temperature from Span and Wagner 1996), so Psat is in bar.
# Temperature ranges are NOT printed in the reproduction. Numerical comparison with Span and Wagner (1996) eq. (3.12)
# (this survey, 2026-09-25): CO2-1 is within 0.52 % of it from 145 to 195 K, -0.93 % at 200 K, -3.9 % at the triple point,
# +11 % at 120 K; CO2-2 is within 0.62 % from 195 K to the triple point, +1.1 % at 190 K, +19 % at 160 K. CO2-1 is the
# low-temperature branch and CO2-2 the branch near the triple point; the exact limits must be read from the original
# paper (owner request list). No uncertainty is stated for the fits.
# Digits verbatim from a 170 dpi render of the page (the text layer agrees for these two rows).
# Role: holdout for the P4 solid CO2 model (G4 sublimation-pressure target), not a model input.
